about: What each colour name must look like, for the eval checks. Written from general colour definitions (Wikipedia colour articles, CSS, Pantone), never derived from the model's output. Two colour spaces are used. Without a 'space' key (the v1.1 definitions): hue is HSV hue in degrees (a range like [335, 3] wraps round through 0), saturation is HSV saturation 0-1, lightness is CIE L* 0-100. With "space": "hsl" (v1.2): hue in degrees, saturation and lightness are HSL, in %. Method 'references': the span of the reference colours, widened by fixed tolerances (hue 10 deg; saturation 0.15 HSV or 15 points HSL; lightness 10 L* or 10 points HSL) and rounded outward. Method 'description': only one standard reference, or the common meaning differs from the reference, so the range follows the written description. Method 'review' (v1.2): the range was set after reviewing the v1.1 renders, where the v1.1 reference colour looked wrong in the image. 'must_fail' lists colours the range must reject. tests/test_eval_checks.py checks that every reference falls inside its range and every must_fail colour outside. The out-of-table colours (rust, ochre, fuchsia, periwinkle, sapphire) are deliberately NOT in data/colours.json and must never be added to it: they measure what the model knows on its own. v2 step 3 added five more held-out names (vermilion, marigold, chartreuse, prussian blue, amethyst), because the first five had been looked at across many sessions; their ranges were written from general colour knowledge before any run, and they appear in no data/ table, the prompt, the schema, the dev set or any other eval sentence (a test checks). 'pink' is only used for a backdrop the sentence names.

emerald.description: The gemstone green: a deep, strong, slightly bluish jewel green.

must_fail.why: Wikipedia: Emerald (color). In the v1.1 render it reads as bright grass green, not a deep jewel green.
v1's emerald: a plain mid green (hue 140).
Wikipedia: Sage (color). In the v1.1 render it reads as olive/khaki, not grey-green (hue 55).

crimson.description: A strong, deep red leaning slightly towards blue.

wine.description: The colour of red wine: a dark red with a hint of purple (burgundy).

gold.description: Metallic gold as used in packaging: a warm, slightly muted yellow-orange. CSS 'gold' (#FFD700) is deliberately not a reference: Wikipedia lists it as 'Gold (web) (Golden)', a saturated golden yellow, not the metallic colour packaging means.

navy.description: A very dark blue. Only one standard reference (CSS navy, which is at the extreme: pure, fully saturated), so the range follows the description: blue hue, clearly saturated, very dark.

blush.description: A soft, pale pink, as 'blush' and 'blush pink' are used in fashion, interiors and packaging. Crayola's 'Blush' (#DE5D83) is a much deeper rose, so the range follows the common meaning: pink to warm pink, low saturation, light.

champagne.description: The drink: a very pale, warm beige.

rust.description: The colour of iron rust: a dark reddish orange-brown. Only one standard reference, so the range follows the description: orange-red to orange, clearly coloured (not a grey-brown), dark to mid. Lighter than that is terracotta or orange.

ochre.description: The earth pigment: a warm orange-brown to golden yellow-brown. Only one standard reference (Wikipedia's ochre, at the orange end; yellow ochre is more golden), so the range follows the description: orange to golden, earthy rather than fully saturated, mid lightness.

must_fail.why: mustard (Wikipedia: Mustard (color)): brighter and fully saturated

fuchsia.description: The flower: a vivid purplish pink to pinkish purple.

periwinkle.description: The flower: a pale blue with a touch of violet. Only one standard reference, so the range follows the description: blue to blue-violet, pale.

sapphire.description: The gemstone: a deep, strong blue.

references.source: Wikipedia: Shades of blue, Sapphire (Maerz and Paul)
Wikipedia: Shades of blue, Sapphire blue (ISCC-NBS)

vermilion.description: The pigment (cinnabar red): a vivid red-orange, clearly more orange than a pure red. The references sit close together, but ten degrees round them would take in pure red, so the range follows the description: red-orange hues, strongly saturated, mid lightness. Pure red (hue 0) is red, not vermilion; lighter is coral or salmon.

marigold.description: The flower: a warm, vivid golden orange-yellow. Only one standard reference, so the range follows the description: orange-yellow hues, strongly saturated, mid lightness. Paler is mustard or lemon, more yellow is yellow, duller is tan.

chartreuse.description: The liqueur: a vivid yellow-green. Two standard meanings, the traditional chartreuse yellow and the CSS chartreuse green; the range covers both, between yellow and green, strongly saturated, mid lightness. Pure yellow (hue 60) and pure green (hue 120) are not chartreuse; a muted yellow-green is pistachio or olive.

prussian blue.description: The pigment: a very dark, deep blue leaning a little towards cyan. Only one standard reference, so the range follows the description: blue hues on the cyan side of pure blue, clearly coloured, very dark. Navy is a purer blue, teal is green-blue, charcoal is grey; sapphire and royal blue are lighter.

must_fail.why: sapphire (Wikipedia: Shades of blue, Maerz and Paul): too light

amethyst.description: The gemstone: a medium to deep violet-purple. Only one standard reference, so the range follows the description: violet hues, clearly coloured, mid to dark. Paler is lavender, lilac or mauve; redder is plum or purple; bluer is periwinkle.

pink.description: Plain pink, for a backdrop the sentence names: light red to purplish red, clearly tinted.

references.source: Wikipedia: Shades of pink, Pale pink (ISCC-NBS)
